owner_posts.post_text: Missed the deadline? You still have routes. Belated return under 139(4): until 31 December, with a late fee. Updated return under 139(8A): up to 24 months from the end of the assessment year, with additional tax. The sooner you file, the lower the cost. Don't let a missed date turn into years of silence. Educational, not tax advice. Digital card:

Selling Indian property as an NRI? Mind the TDS. The buyer must deduct TDS under Section 195 - and by default it is on the full sale value, not just the gain. Apply for a lower-deduction certificate (Section 197) before closing, and the TDS drops to the actual tax on the actual gain. Start it 2-3 months ahead - it is the single biggest cash-flow lever in an NRI sale. Educational, not tax advice. Digital card:

The audit trail mandate is live - is your software compliant? Companies must use accounting software with an edit log (audit trail) that cannot be disabled - effective for financial years from 1 April 2023. The auditor now reports on it under Rule 11(g). If your books run on a tool without a tamper-proof log, fix it before the audit, not during. Educational, not tax advice. Digital card:

Investors read your cap table before your pitch. Messy ESOP grants, undocumented SAFEs, missing board approvals - these surface in due diligence and slow or reprice a round. Keep the register of members, the option register and PAS-3 filings current as you go. A clean cap table is a quiet signal that the rest of the house is in order. Educational, not tax advice. Digital card:

Which ITR form is yours? ITR-1: salary + one house + interest, income up to Rs 50L. ITR-2: capital gains, multiple properties, foreign assets. ITR-3: business or professional income, F&O. ITR-4: presumptive (44AD/44ADA). The wrong form gets your return treated as defective. Choose by your income types, not last year's habit. Educational, not tax advice. Digital card:

Your society deducts TDS too. Payments to contractors - housekeeping, security, repairs - attract TDS under 194C; professional fees under 194J, once you cross the thresholds. Deduct, deposit, file quarterly returns, issue certificates. Societies often miss this and face disallowance plus interest. The committee is responsible, not just the manager. Educational, not tax advice. Digital card:

Co-founder equity without vesting is a risk. If a co-founder leaves in year one with fully-vested shares, the cap table is stuck. Reverse vesting fixes it - shares vest over time, unvested ones return to the company. Lock it into the Shareholders' Agreement and Articles at incorporation, not after a dispute. The cheapest time to agree exit terms is before anyone wants to exit. Educational, not tax advice. Digital card:

Before you file, reconcile three statements. 26AS (tax credits), AIS (annual information), TIS (taxpayer summary). They now capture interest, dividends, securities trades and large spends. File a return that contradicts your AIS and a 143(1) intimation is likely. Download all three, match them to your books, then file. It is the best way to avoid a notice. Educational, not tax advice. Digital card:

Input Tax Credit - where businesses lose money. Claim only what appears in your GSTR-2B, match it to your purchase register, and ensure your supplier actually filed. Missing invoices, blocked credits (Section 17(5)), and supplier defaults are the usual leaks. Reconcile 2B every month, not at year-end. Lost ITC is real cash gone. Educational, not tax advice. Digital card:

The 180-day trap new founders miss. After incorporating a Pvt Ltd, you must file INC-20A (commencement of business) within 180 days - after depositing the subscription capital. Miss it and the company can be struck off, plus penalties. A small filing with a big consequence. Diarise it on day one. Educational, not tax advice. Digital card:
